[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering torch.nn Module, Parameters, and State Dict in PyTorch"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Building deep learning models in PyTorch requires a solid understanding of how neural network layers are structured, how weights are tracked, and how models are saved and loaded. At the core of this architecture are three fundamental components: torch.nn.Module, Parameters, and the State Dict."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. The torch.nn.Module Class"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The torch.nn.Module is the base class for all neural network modules in PyTorch. Your custom models should always subclass this class. A well-designed module typically defines layers in the __init__ method and specifies the forward pass computation in the forward method."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class SimpleMLP(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, hidden_dim, output_dim):
        super(SimpleMLP, self).__init__()
        self.layer1 = nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU()
        self.layer2 = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.layer1(x)
        x = self.relu(x)
        x = self.layer2(x)
        return x

model = SimpleMLP(input_dim=10, hidden_dim=20, output_dim=2)
print(model)"},{"order":6,"type":"heading","text":"2. Understanding Parameters (torch.nn.Parameter)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Parameters are tensors that are subclasses of torch.Tensor and are implicitly registered as model parameters when assigned as attributes of an nn.Module. This means they will be tracked by optimizers and included in the model's state dictionary."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"nn.Parameter automatically sets requires_grad=True by default."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"You can inspect all parameters in a model using model.parameters() or model.named_parameters()."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"class CustomLayerWithParameter(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, size):
        super().__init__()
        # Registering a custom trainable weight vector
        self.custom_weight = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(size))

    def forward(self, x):
        return x * self.custom_weight

custom_layer = CustomLayerWithParameter(5)
for name, param in custom_layer.named_parameters():
    print(f'Parameter Name: {name}, Shape: {param.shape}')"},{"order":11,"type":"heading","text":"3. The State Dict (state_dict)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"The state_dict is a Python dictionary object that maps each layer to its corresponding parameter tensor (such as weights and biases). Only layers with trainable parameters (like nn.Linear, nn.Conv2d) and persistent buffers (like running mean in nn.BatchNorm2d) have entries in the model's state_dict."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"# Inspecting the state dictionary keys and shapes
model = SimpleMLP(10, 20, 2)
state_dict = model.state_dict()

for key, tensor in state_dict.items():
    print(f'{key}: {tensor.size()}')"},{"order":14,"type":"heading","text":"4. Saving and Loading Models"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the state_dict is a standard Python dictionary, serializing it using torch.save() is the recommended, lightweight approach for saving trained models in PyTorch. To restore the model, instantiate the architecture and load the state dictionary using load_state_dict()."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"# Saving the state dictionary
torch.save(model.state_dict(), 'model_weights.pth')

# Loading the state dictionary into a new model instance
loaded_model = SimpleMLP(10, 20, 2)
loaded_model.load_state_dict(torch.load('model_weights.pth'))
loaded_model.eval()
print('Model successfully loaded from state_dict!')"},{"order":17,"type":"heading","text":"Summary"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"nn.Module organizes your neural network structure and tracks parameters."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"nn.Parameter designates tensors as learnable variables required for backpropagation."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"state_dict handles parameter persistence, allowing you to easily save and load weights."}]
